name: created-then-removed-assertion-scope
body: Three limits. (1) The save's `no pending changes` report is written to the coordinator process's stdout while the client reply is the fixed `Session saved`, so the no-op is pinned by durable state (no node file, no commit, empty ledger, no dirty row, absent read), not by wording; upgrade if the message itself must ever be pinned — capture the session process's stdout — but the test should stay state-based even then. (2) The "no dirty row" read is scoped to the `Requirement` table, the only table the create-then-remove fixture touches; widen it if a later task makes the test admit mutations on more than one node table. (3) The remove-then-re-add arm asserts the ledger row and the written-back file, not the post-save ledger drain, and `Coordinator::save` still builds its delete set from the buffered changes rather than from the ledger — so the "save would delete the re-added file" half is judgemental until phase 2 derives the delete set from the ledger; at that point the post-save `PendingRemoval` == 0 assertion should also cover the drain.
